newsitem.title: USA: Guards grab gunman at Pentagon's front door.
newsitem.headline: Guards grab gunman at Pentagon's front door.

text.p: A gunman wielding a loaded Beretta pistol and demanding to see the "admiral in charge" was wrestled to the ground Tuesday as he tried to enter the Pentagon.
The gunman, identified as Raymond Steve Maestas, 36, of West Covina, Calif., occupation unknown, was taken into custody and no one was injured in the incident, the Defence Department said.
The incident, at 8:15 a.m., prompted Army bomb disposal experts to roll out a robot to check the suspect's car for explosives. None were found.
Initial checks showed Maestas had a criminal record, but details were not immediately available, Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters.

Maestas, not known to have served in the military, was handcuffed and held in a special holding pen at the Pentagon, across the Potomac River from Washington, before being scheduled to be sent to nearby Alexandria, Va., to be booked on unspecified charges.

Lacking an identification pass that would have let him past security guards at a front desk, Maestas "asked to speak to the admiral in charge. And then he asked to speak to the 'vice admiral' about a car theft," Bacon said.

"This wasn't the normal guy coming to work," he added. When a security officer took him aside for further checks, Maestas reached into his knapsack and pulled out a loaded 9 mm Beretta pistol, Bacon said.
After he was disarmed by two guards manning the security checkpoint at the Pentagon's Mall entrance, security personnel found a key to the rented car Maestas had driven.

The Army then deployed a robot to try to turn the key in the car in case it was wired to explode. The robot failed to open the door, but an army expert in bomb-protection gear did so and found no explosives, Bacon said.
"And they also found no indication of what he was doing or why," he said.
